newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money trade picks up on better supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money trade picks up on better supply.

text.p: Croatian money market trade picked up on Friday morning thanks to better supply, following a pre-Christmas shortage of kuna, dealers said.
"The trade today has been much better than before the Christmas holidays," one dealer told Reuters.
She said all the 34.5 million kuna demand had been met as banks offered funds from the start of morning trade.
Most loans were call money at a steady rate of 11 percent with one loan to an insurer being granted at 12 percent.
Two short-term placements were made at 12 and 15 percent and one 90-day loan at 17 percent.
Tuesday's overnight trade, the last before Christmas, totalled only 1.9 million kuna with one bank borrowing money to square its position. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
